chapter: Irish Channel youth, newspapers and McDonogh 35
title: High school hangouts and working for tailor Lewis Silvers
summary: He went to Rampart Street and West Bank clubs, and Lewis Silvers the tailor gave him his first zoot suit, a job and money for Xavier.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Now if you get down to the real brass tacks, where did you guys go for a good time when you were in high school? Where did you take a girl when you were in high school? Thelma Brown.

I used to go down on Ramport Street and when I would go on the other side of the river I would go over to Coleman's place over on the West Bank of the river and I would also go to Copper's down the West Bank of the river and I also used to hang out. And I also used to hang out, they had a place up in Harvey called Lewis. Lewis was a bad Lemento, was an Italian type of guy. He had a nice club up there in Marrero. And he had black bartenders, white bartenders working for him back in the 40s and 50s. And we used to have some good times. Even in the 30s when I had to sneak into place. And now as I started working and making a few dollars working down on Ramport Street, I started selling clothes. And I was partly raised by Jews. That's why today I can speak some of the Hebrew and Jewish language. I can count in the Jewish language very good. I read a little Hebrew now and then. The Jewish people were very nice to me coming up. Because Lewis Silvers, who was the guy that had best tailors at that particular time. I can remember my first Zoot suit was made by Lewis Silvers. That's how I happened to get involved into the tailoring business. Because a fella by the name of Warren took me down there. And, you know, he made the first suit for me. And then Lewis took a liking to me and said, boy, you want to work just like that? I said, yes, sir. I started working for Lewis Silvers today. Lewis Silvers is dead. But he gave me probably the first $100 I had to put on a deposit to pay my way to start college back at Xavier. And not only that, I never had to worry about food. I never had to worry about just any time I had a problem. Lewis was always there. In fact, the first automobile I bought, the first $25 I had when I bought a 37 Chevrolet came from Lewis Silvers. And the thing I wanted, old Lewis was there. He and his wife. And today, his adopted son is an attorney here. Lewis Silvers, Jr. He's an attorney in the city of New Orleans. And he and I are very, very good friends.
